title: Performance of the American Heart Association (AHA) 14-Point Evaluation Versus Electrocardiography for the Cardiovascular Screening of High School Athletes: A Prospective Study
publisher: Journal of the American Heart Association
claims: In a prospective study of high school athletes, the AHA 14-point evaluation produced a high number of false-positive results with poor sensitivity and very low positive predictive value.
ECG screening outperformed the AHA 14-point questionnaire by all measures of statistical performance when interpreted by experienced clinicians.
The authors recommended that routine use of the AHA 14-point evaluation or similar history-based questionnaires as the principal screening tool should be reevaluated.
